raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #61998

## Overview

The zeroth pass of `_topk_topp_kernel` picks the gather pivot with a Gaussian
quantile (`avg + std * sigma`) fitted to the **first 8192 logits only**. On
real logits (MiMo-V2.6 measurements in the issue) the head of the row carries
systematically higher values, and skewed rows break the Gaussian fit entirely;
the gather then returns fewer than `k` candidates and the row falls back to a
full-vocab ternary search, 3-6x slower per row, stalling every other row in
the batch.

This PR replaces the Gaussian estimate with an **order statistic of a strided
sample taken across the whole row**:

- Sample `S = BLOCK_SIZE / 4` logits uniformly across the row (one lane every
  `NUM_TILES * 4` vocab entries), so head bias cannot skew the estimate.
- Target `m = max(8, ceil(4 * k * S / V))` — the m-th largest sample value,
  found with a 12-step in-register binary search (no extra global memory
  traffic). The 4x margin over `k` keeps the gathered set small (a few
  hundred entries at V=152576) while reliably covering `k`.
- When the sample holds no finite logits (grammar bitmask hiding most of the
  vocab), the pivot degenerates to `+inf` (gather nothing) and the existing
  full-row fallback search runs with its finite, well-scaled bounds. A
  sentinel like `-1e30` would instead poison the buffer-search range and never
  converge (found via a fuzz case, fixed in `test_topk_pivot_all_masked_sample`).
- The Gaussian path, both sigma tables and the table upload, are removed.

## Claims

- Rows whose gather previously failed no longer take the full-vocab fallback:
  **3-6x lower latency per affected row**; batches containing one such row
  stop stalling.
- Gather-healthy rows are within noise of the previous numbers (the strided
  sample is a quarter of the old first-tile read).

## Validation

A800-SXM4-80GB, V=152576, CUDA graph, median of 50 runs, issue's repro script
(`zipf, sorted ids` and `two modes` are the distributions whose rows failed
the old gather; the `gather` column in the repro is the *old* diagnostic):

| rows | B | k | main top-k | this PR top-k |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| two modes | 64 | 50 | 923.6 us | 182.3 us |
| two modes | 64 | 200 | 1062.9 us | 188.4 us |
| zipf, sorted ids | 64 | 200 | 1203.2 us | 189.4 us |
| 63 zipf + 1 two-modes | 64 | 64 | 620.5 us | 189.4 us |
| zipf, permuted (healthy) | 64 | 200 | 232.4 us | 237.6 us |
| zipf, permuted (healthy) | 1 | 50 | 176.1 us | 194.6 us |

Correctness:
- Existing `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`: **154 passed** (one
  grammar-mask case initially caught a real degenerate-pivot bug in this
  change; fixed by the `+inf` sentinel).
- New `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_pivot_order_statistic.py`: 8 passed —
  exact-mask comparison against a PyTorch reference over the failing
  distributions (zipf-sorted, two-modes, uniform, sparse grammar masks).
- Fuzz over 5 distributions x 3 batch sizes x 6 k values: 0 mismatches.

## Details

- The buffer search and the top-p stage are untouched; only the pivot choice
  in the zeroth pass changes, so the fallback path remains as a safety net.
- Limitation: like the old code, the sample is a lattice, so adversarial
  distributions can still miss `k` by a few tokens; the fallback search then
  runs exactly as before (correct, slower). The 4x margin makes this
  measure-by-measure rare on real logits.

🚀

**Update: real-model E2E validation** — following the discussion in #61998 about coverage beyond synthetic data, I ran the fix on captured decode logits from three models plus a full vLLM generation run. Setup: A800-SXM4-80GB, wheel 0.31.0 kernel with only the zeroth-pass replacement applied (identical logic to this PR), VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0.

**1. Real-logit fallback rates (stock zeroth-pass emulation, the issue's n_outliers).** ~250 decode rows per model, teacher-forced on long code/expository prompts:

| model | V | k=20 | k=64 | k=200 | k=500 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B | 151936 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 10.0% | 81.2% |
| Qwen3-8B | 151936 | 0.0% | 0.8% | 7.2% | 73.6% |
| MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B | 248320 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 3.4% | 72.0% |

The issue's MiMo capture found 43%/86% at k=200/500; the V2.6 distill shows the same class of failure (72% at k=500) at somewhat lower rates. Default-config models (k=20) essentially never fall back — consistent with the issue's 0.07% at k=20 — so the win is for larger top-k configs.

**2. Kernel latency on the captured real rows** (CUDA graph, median of 50, B=64, top-k + top-p=0.95):

| model | k | stock | fixed | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B | 20 | 329.7 us | 344.1 us | 0.96x (healthy rows, +4%) |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 200 | 1010.7 us | 346.6 us | **2.9x** |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 500 | 1095.7 us | 354.3 us | **3.1x** |
| Qwen3-8B | 20 | 311.3 us | 337.9 us | 0.92x (healthy rows, +9%) |
| Qwen3-8B | 200 | 931.8 us | 349.2 us | **2.7x** |
| Qwen3-8B | 500 | 1018.9 us | 352.3 us | **2.9x** |
| MiMo-9B | 20 | 531.5 us | 546.8 us | 0.97x (healthy rows, +3%) |
| MiMo-9B | 200 | 1570.8 us | 556.0 us | **2.8x** |
| MiMo-9B | 500 | 1762.3 us | 558.1 us | **3.2x** |

**3. Mask equality.** For every model and every k tested, the stock and fixed kernels produce bit-identical output masks over all captured rows (verified with torch.equal over the full [rows, V] output, including the fallback rows).

**4. Full vLLM generation run** (Qwen3-8B, 64 concurrent requests x 192 tokens, identical warmup in both runs):

| k | stock sampler/call | fixed sampler/call | stock tok/s | fixed tok/s |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 200 | 606.7 us | 378.6 us | 4147 | 4225 (+1.9%) |
| 500 | 990.6 us | 395.9 us | 4059 | 4198 (+3.4%) |

The sampler is a small fraction of a decode step for an 8B dense model on A800, so the E2E gain is modest at this scale — but per-step sampler time drops 1.6x (k=200) to 2.5x (k=500) with zero output changes. The gain grows with batch size and vocab (rejection-sampling verification batches), where the whole batch waits on the slowest row.

One note on healthy rows: the fixed zeroth pass costs +3-9% on B=64 k=20 vs stock here (the strided sample + in-register binary search vs one tile's mean/std). That is the trade the issue's emulation predicted at 2-4us/kernel-scale on B300; on A800 at this batch size it is ~15-26us per call. If maintainers want, the gather could dispatch on `k` (Gaussian pivot for k <= ~32 where it never fails, order statistic above) — happy to benchmark that variant if there's interest.

Repro: capture script + kernel A/B harness at https://gist.github.com/hjh123445/ — will link once uploaded; methodology is exactly the issue's n_outliers emulation + CUDA-graph replay timing on teacher-forced decode rows.

**Addendum: full issue-repro matrix (all 30 cells) + k=1000.** Ran the issue's exact repro script unmodified (same seeds, same row types, V=152576) against the stock wheel 0.31.0 kernel and the zeroth-pass replacement from this PR, back to back on the same A800. This covers the cells the earlier tables skipped (B=16, the top-k+top-p column with the split top-p pipeline, and all k values including k=1000 on real captured rows).

Note: the `gather` FAIL column in the fixed run is the script's *stock-pivot diagnostic* (n_outliers emulates the Gaussian zeroth pass only) — it marks which rows the stock kernel falls back on. The fixed kernel's latency column shows those rows now take the fast path.

**top-k only (median of 50, CUDA graph, us):**

| rows | B | k | stock | fixed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| zipf, permuted | 1 | 50 | 188.4 | 201.7 |
| zipf, permuted | 1 | 200 | 193.5 | 195.6 |
| zipf, permuted | 16 | 64 | 194.6 | 203.8 |
| zipf, permuted | 64 | 200 | 248.8 | 262.1 |
| zipf, sorted ids | 1 | 200 | 616.4 | 198.7 |
| zipf, sorted ids | 16 | 200 | 899.1 | 206.8 |
| zipf, sorted ids | 64 | 200 | 1265.7 | 216.1 |
| two modes | 1 | 50 | 549.9 | 158.7 |
| two modes | 16 | 64 | 1027.1 | 172.0 |
| two modes | 64 | 200 | 1127.4 | 215.0 |
| 63 zipf-perm + 1 two-modes | 64 | 64 | 647.2 | 214.0 |

(omitted cells behave as expected; full table can be rerun from the issue's script with any kernel file path.)

**top-k + top-p=0.95 (includes the split top-p pipeline at B<=64):**

| rows | B | k | stock | fixed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| zipf, sorted ids | 64 | 200 | 1469.4 | 302.1 |
| two modes | 64 | 200 | 1333.2 | 242.7 |
| two modes | 1 | 50 | 734.2 | 182.3 |
| 63 zipf-perm + 1 | 64 | 64 | 852.0 | 240.6 |

**k=1000 on real captured rows** (Qwen3-0.6B decode logits, B=64, top-k+top-p; the issue's emulation tested k up to 1000 but its repro script stopped at 200):

| k | stock | fixed | masks identical |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1000 | 1125.4 us | 401.4 us (2.8x) | yes (torch.equal over all rows) |

Healthy-row cost at this batch size stays in the +4-7% band across all k (e.g. k=50: 332.8 -> 346.1 us; k=64: 335.9 -> 349.2 us).

**Reproducibility** — the scripts behind every table in this PR are now in one place: [hjh123445/vllm-topk-order-statistic-pivot/tree/main/bench](https://github.com/hjh123445/oss_contribution_workspace/tree/main/vllm_61998_bench). Mapping from tables to commands:

| PR table | script | command |
|---|---|---|
| synthetic matrix (all 30 cells + 63+1 batch) | `repro_issue.py` | the issue's own script, unmodified, pointed at either kernel file |
| real-logit fallback rates | `capture_logits2.py` | teacher-forced decode rows from any HF model, + the stock zeroth-pass emulation inside `time_kernel.py` |
| kernel latency on real rows (incl. k=1000) | `time_kernel.py` | `python time_kernel.py rows.pt --k <k> --bs 64` (CUDA graph, median of 50) |
| mask equality | both kernels on all rows, `torch.equal` on outputs | included in the harness flow |
| E2E generation throughput | `e2e_generate.py` | `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 python e2e_generate.py <model> <tag> <k>` |

Methodology notes (also in the harness README): timings are CUDA-graph replay medians of 50, matching the issue's methodology; the E2E hook requires single-process mode so the sampler patch lands in-process; warmup covers the full batch to compile all batch-size specializations before measurement. For the A/B, the stock side is the released wheel 0.31.0 kernel and the fixed side is that same file with only the zeroth-pass region replaced by this PR's logic — so the comparison isolates the change and no other main-branch drift.

**Update: reworked implementation + shared-protocol benchmark (addresses the review feedback in #61998 and incorporates the fallback design from #62760).**

Rework summary (commit 8e6478c):
1. **Zeroth pass keeps the Gaussian quantile** (the paper's method), but samples **four quarters of the row** instead of tile 0 — the layout bias the issue identified. The stock 0.15 safety discount is kept: with unbiased sampling, the gather fails <1% on real decode rows at every k measured (Qwen3-8B: 0.0%/0.8%/0.8% at k=20/50/64; 7.6% at k=200; 86% only at k=1000).
2. **When the gather under-covers k**, re-gather once at a distribution-free pivot into the per-program buffer, then run the ternary search entirely in the buffer (L2-resident — the fallback shape from #62760):
   - dense rows: the m-th largest of a 2048-lane strided whole-row sample, m = max(8, ceil(4kS/V)) — no distribution assumption, so it covers the skewed rows the Gaussian cannot;
   - sparse rows (grammar masks, where the sample may see no finite logit): the row minimum, which collects every finite candidate — the row is known to hold >= k finite logits (upstream short-circuit), so the buffer always covers k.
3. Small k is untouched relative to main: same read volume (8192 lanes, now in four coalesced segments), same discount, same tight gather.

**Shared protocol, same A800 for all three kernels** (wheel 0.31.0 + single-file swap; captured teacher-forced decode rows, ~250 rows/model; CUDA-graph replay, median of 50; top-k + top-p=0.95):

*Synthetic (the issue's repro rows, B=64):*

| rows | k | main | #62760 | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| zipf, permuted | 50 | 271.4 | 430.1 | **272.4** |
| zipf, permuted | 200 | 345.1 | 526.3 | **349.7** |
| zipf, sorted ids | 200 | 1280.5 | 238.6 | 292.9 |
| two modes | 200 | 1350.7 | 1549.3 | **350.2** |
| two modes | 1000 | 1499.1 | 1728.5 | **469.0** |

*Real decode rows (B=64):*

| model | k | main | #62760 | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 20 | 738.8 | 840.7 | 717.1 * |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 200 | 2181.1 | 1084.4 | **774.1** |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 1000 | 2555.9 | 997.4 | **895.5** |
| Qwen3-8B | 200 | 1196.0 | 867.3 | **772.1** |
| Qwen3-8B | 1000 | 2500.6 | 908.3 | **920.6** |
| MiMo-V2.6-9B | 200 | 2217.0 | 1470.5 | **1315.8** |

*E2E (vLLM offline generation, 64 concurrent, sampler-path kernel time per step):*

| model | k | main | #62760 | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 200 | 719.6 | 408.8 | **386.5** |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 1000 | 955.0 | **418.9** | 429.2 |
| Qwen3-8B | 200 | 606.7 | 399.2 | **390.7** |
| Qwen3-8B | 1000 | 990.6 | **410.6** | 454.1 |

Where #62760 wins (small-k healthy rows on A10/L40S in its own table, and k=1000 E2E here by ~5-10%) the difference traces to the 0.5 discount: it removes the k=1000 re-gather entirely on real rows at the cost of a ~10x larger candidate set on every other row. A k-dispatched discount (0.15 for k < some threshold, 0.50 above) recovers both ends if reviewers prefer.

**Correctness**: the official `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py` passes 132/132 on this branch; masks are bit-identical to main on all captured real rows and all synthetic rows except the documented near-tie boundary cases (single tokens at prob ~1e-4, same class as stock-vs-#62760). The sparse-row fallback is covered by `test_topk_pivot_all_masked_sample` and the `all_masked`/`grammar` cases here; the dense-row re-gather by the `two modes` rows.

**Correction to the comparison tables: re-benchmarked against the latest #62760 head (46d3ab83, "add finite logits fallback for extreme skewness")** — my earlier tables used the 75b86df9 head. The new commit adds an all-finite re-gather when the avg_logit re-gather also under-covers, which improves the skewed-row case. Same A800, same protocol, all three kernels swapped into the same wheel:

*Synthetic (issue repro rows, B=64, top-k + top-p=0.95, CUDA-graph median of 50):*

| rows | k | main | #62760@46d3ab8 | this PR@8e6478c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| zipf, permuted | 50 | 271.4 | 433.2 | **272.4** |
| zipf, permuted | 200 | 345.1 | 528.4 | **352.3** |
| zipf, permuted | 1000 | 421.9 | 625.7 | **428.0** |
| zipf, sorted ids | 200 | 1279.0 | **241.7** | 293.9 |
| two modes | 50 | 1218.6 | 1092.6 | **349.2** |
| two modes | 200 | 1349.6 | 1385.5 | **350.2** |
| two modes | 1000 | 1499.1 | 1494.0 | **469.0** |

*Real decode rows (B=64, same protocol):*

| model | k | main | #62760@46d3ab8 | this PR@8e6478c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 200 | 1818.6 | 1114.1 | **911.4** |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 1000 | 2556.4 | 1023.0 | **897.0** |
| Qwen3-8B | 200 | 1195.0 | 894.0 | **772.1** |
| Qwen3-8B | 1000 | 2501.1 | 933.9 | **922.6** |
| MiMo-V2.6-9B | 200 | 2211.8 | 1718.3 | **1534.5** |
| MiMo-V2.6-9B | 1000 | 4353.5 | **1489.9** | 1620.0 |

The remaining #62760 wins are zipf-sorted at k>=200 (its larger 0.5-discount gather skips the re-gather there) and MiMo at k=1000 (~8%); the remaining costs are the healthy-row 0.5-discount overhead (433 vs 271 at k=50) and the two-modes row mean-gather sweep (~119k entries) that the new finite re-gather then has to undo — the order-statistic re-gather in this PR goes straight to a tight pivot instead. Both correct on all 80 distribution/param cells (identical masks except the documented top-p near-tie boundary class, which also appears between main and either PR).

**Architecture note** (to make the tiered structure of the reworked fallback explicit, following the discussion with #62760):

```
zeroth pass: Gaussian quantile over a 4-quarter coalesced sample  (the paper's
             estimator, layout-bias fixed per #62760; stock 0.15 discount)
  ├─ gather covers k  (>99% of real decode rows at every k measured)
  │    → search the gathered buffer (unchanged fast path)
  └─ gather under-covers k
       → tier 2: re-gather once at the order-statistic pivot
         (m-th largest of a 2048-lane strided whole-row sample, 4x margin
          over k — no distribution assumption, covers skewed rows)
         ├─ dense rows (num_finite_total > 2*BLOCK_SIZE): the sample has
         │  ~450+ finite lanes, so the m-th order statistic is reliable
         └─ sparse rows (grammar masks): the sample may hold too few finite
            lanes to estimate anything — take the row minimum instead,
            which collects every finite candidate. The row is guaranteed
            to hold >= k finite logits (upstream num_finite_total <= k
            short-circuit), so this always covers k
       → all ternary-search iterations then run inside the re-gathered
         buffer (L2-resident, #62760's fallback shape)
```

Each tier only pays when the previous one fails: normal rows cost the same as main plus the (already-present) 8192-lane read, now in four segments; skewed rows pay one extra full sweep for the re-gather; sparse rows pay one more. Nothing ever falls back to the 18-iteration full-vocab DRAM search — that path is gone.

Hi @hjh123445, #60104 fixes a separate correctness issue in the standalone top-p block changed here. Sampling four quarters improves the initial estimate, but a sufficiently large unsampled logit can still overflow exp(logits - max_sample) and make top-p keep the whole row. #60104 raises that reference as needed, rescales the accumulated sum, and matches boundary duplicates in probability space.

I'm keeping that normalization repair and its regression tests in #60104. Could we coordinate the overlapping edits so both changes are preserved, whichever lands first?

We've rebased #62596 onto current main (commit 3d3a8ec2) — the standalone top-p zeroth pass is back to stock, so the two diffs no longer share any lines. Whichever lands first, the other rebases cleanly.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,111 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for the order-statistic gather pivot in the combined top-k/top-p
+Triton kernel (#61998).
+
+The kernel's zeroth pass used to estimate the gather pivot as a Gaussian
+quantile (avg + std * sigma) computed from the first 8192 logits only. On
+real logits that pivot is frequently too high, the gather returns fewer than
+k candidates, and the row falls back to a full-vocab ternary search. The
+pivot is now the m-th largest value of a strided sample taken across the
+whole row, which keeps the gathered set small on every distribution tried
+here while never under-covering k.
+
+These tests exercise the distributions where the old pivot fails and compare
+the Triton mask against an exact PyTorch reference.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.sample.ops.topk_topp_triton import apply_top_k_top_p_triton
+
+VOCAB = 152576
+DEVICES = ["cuda"]
+
+
+def _reference_topk_mask(logits: torch.Tensor, k: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Exact top-k mask: keep the k largest logits (stable tie order)."""
+    out = logits.clone()
+    order = torch.argsort(-logits, dim=-1, stable=True)
+    keep = torch.zeros_like(logits, dtype=torch.bool)
+    keep.scatter_(1, order[:, :k], True)
+    out[~keep] = float("-inf")
+    return out
+
+
+def _make_rows(kind: str, batch: int, vocab: int, device: str, seed: int = 0):
+    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
+    if kind == "zipf_sorted":
+        # High logits concentrated at low token ids: the head-biased sample
+        # statistics of the old pivot are wrong here.
+        x = -torch.log1p(torch.arange(vocab, device=device).float())
+        return (x + 2.0 * torch.randn(batch, vocab, device=device, generator=g))
+    if kind == "two_modes":
+        # Bimodal: the inflated std pushes the Gaussian pivot above the row
+        # max, so the old gather collects nothing.
+        x = torch.randn(batch, vocab, device=device, generator=g)
+        return x - 10.0 * (torch.rand(batch, vocab, device=device, generator=g) < 0.2)
+    if kind == "uniform":
+        return torch.rand(batch, vocab, device=device, generator=g)
+    if kind == "grammar_sparse":
+        # 99% of the vocab masked to -inf, like a grammar bitmask: the strided
+        # sample may contain no finite logits at all.
+        x = torch.randn(batch, vocab, device=device, generator=g)
+        keep = torch.rand(batch, vocab, device=device, generator=g) > 0.99
+        return torch.where(keep, x, torch.full_like(x, float("-inf")))
+    raise ValueError(kind)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["zipf_sorted", "two_modes", "uniform"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("k", [50, 200])
+def test_topk_pivot_covers_k(kind: str, k: int):
+    """The gather must cover k candidates: exactly k tokens survive."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA unavailable")
+    device = "cuda"
+    x = _make_rows(kind, 16, VOCAB, device)
+    kt = torch.full((16,), k, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    out = apply_top_k_top_p_triton(x.clone(), kt, None)
+    finite = (x > float("-inf")).sum(-1)
+    kept = (out > float("-inf")).sum(-1)
+    assert (kept == torch.minimum(finite, torch.full_like(finite, k))).all()
+    # The kept set must be exactly the k largest values.
+    ref = _reference_topk_mask(x, k)
+    assert torch.equal(out > float("-inf"), ref > float("-inf"))
+
+
+def test_topk_pivot_all_masked_sample():
+    """Rows where the strided sample sees no finite logit must still produce
+    an exact top-k mask via the full-row fallback search."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA unavailable")

+    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0)

+    kt = torch.full((batch,), 3, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    out = apply_top_k_top_p_triton(x.clone(), kt, None)
+    kept = (out > float("-inf")).sum(-1)
+    assert (kept == 3).all()
+    ref = _reference_topk_mask(x, 3)
+    assert torch.equal(out > float("-inf"), ref > float("-inf"))
+
+
+def test_topk_pivot_grammar_masked_keeps_k():
+    """A grammar-style mask (99% masked) with more finite tokens than k."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA unavailable")
+    device = "cuda"
+    x = _make_rows("grammar_sparse", 8, VOCAB, device)
+    kt = torch.full((8,), 200, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    out = apply_top_k_top_p_triton(x.clone(), kt, None)
+    finite = (x > float("-inf")).sum(-1)
+    kept = (out > float("-inf")).sum(-1)
+    # k=200 vs ~1% of 152576 = ~1525 finite: some rows may have fewer than
+    # k finite logits; those must keep every finite token.
+    assert (kept == torch.minimum(finite, torch.full_like(finite, 200))).all()

🚀

**Update: real-model E2E validation** — following the discussion in #61998 about coverage beyond synthetic data, I ran the fix on captured decode logits from three models plus a full vLLM generation run. Setup: A800-SXM4-80GB, wheel 0.31.0 kernel with only the zeroth-pass replacement applied (identical logic to this PR), VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0.

**1. Real-logit fallback rates (stock zeroth-pass emulation, the issue's n_outliers).** ~250 decode rows per model, teacher-forced on long code/expository prompts:

| model | V | k=20 | k=64 | k=200 | k=500 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B | 151936 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 10.0% | 81.2% |
| Qwen3-8B | 151936 | 0.0% | 0.8% | 7.2% | 73.6% |
| MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B | 248320 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 3.4% | 72.0% |

The issue's MiMo capture found 43%/86% at k=200/500; the V2.6 distill shows the same class of failure (72% at k=500) at somewhat lower rates. Default-config models (k=20) essentially never fall back — consistent with the issue's 0.07% at k=20 — so the win is for larger top-k configs.

**2. Kernel latency on the captured real rows** (CUDA graph, median of 50, B=64, top-k + top-p=0.95):

| model | k | stock | fixed | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B | 20 | 329.7 us | 344.1 us | 0.96x (healthy rows, +4%) |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 200 | 1010.7 us | 346.6 us | **2.9x** |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 500 | 1095.7 us | 354.3 us | **3.1x** |
| Qwen3-8B | 20 | 311.3 us | 337.9 us | 0.92x (healthy rows, +9%) |
| Qwen3-8B | 200 | 931.8 us | 349.2 us | **2.7x** |
| Qwen3-8B | 500 | 1018.9 us | 352.3 us | **2.9x** |
| MiMo-9B | 20 | 531.5 us | 546.8 us | 0.97x (healthy rows, +3%) |
| MiMo-9B | 200 | 1570.8 us | 556.0 us | **2.8x** |
| MiMo-9B | 500 | 1762.3 us | 558.1 us | **3.2x** |

**3. Mask equality.** For every model and every k tested, the stock and fixed kernels produce bit-identical output masks over all captured rows (verified with torch.equal over the full [rows, V] output, including the fallback rows).

**4. Full vLLM generation run** (Qwen3-8B, 64 concurrent requests x 192 tokens, identical warmup in both runs):

| k | stock sampler/call | fixed sampler/call | stock tok/s | fixed tok/s |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 200 | 606.7 us | 378.6 us | 4147 | 4225 (+1.9%) |
| 500 | 990.6 us | 395.9 us | 4059 | 4198 (+3.4%) |

The sampler is a small fraction of a decode step for an 8B dense model on A800, so the E2E gain is modest at this scale — but per-step sampler time drops 1.6x (k=200) to 2.5x (k=500) with zero output changes. The gain grows with batch size and vocab (rejection-sampling verification batches), where the whole batch waits on the slowest row.

One note on healthy rows: the fixed zeroth pass costs +3-9% on B=64 k=20 vs stock here (the strided sample + in-register binary search vs one tile's mean/std). That is the trade the issue's emulation predicted at 2-4us/kernel-scale on B300; on A800 at this batch size it is ~15-26us per call. If maintainers want, the gather could dispatch on `k` (Gaussian pivot for k <= ~32 where it never fails, order statistic above) — happy to benchmark that variant if there's interest.

Repro: capture script + kernel A/B harness at https://gist.github.com/hjh123445/ — will link once uploaded; methodology is exactly the issue's n_outliers emulation + CUDA-graph replay timing on teacher-forced decode rows.

**Addendum: full issue-repro matrix (all 30 cells) + k=1000.** Ran the issue's exact repro script unmodified (same seeds, same row types, V=152576) against the stock wheel 0.31.0 kernel and the zeroth-pass replacement from this PR, back to back on the same A800. This covers the cells the earlier tables skipped (B=16, the top-k+top-p column with the split top-p pipeline, and all k values including k=1000 on real captured rows).

Note: the `gather` FAIL column in the fixed run is the script's *stock-pivot diagnostic* (n_outliers emulates the Gaussian zeroth pass only) — it marks which rows the stock kernel falls back on. The fixed kernel's latency column shows those rows now take the fast path.

**Reproducibility** — the scripts behind every table in this PR are now in one place: [hjh123445/vllm-topk-order-statistic-pivot/tree/main/bench](https://github.com/hjh123445/oss_contribution_workspace/tree/main/vllm_61998_bench). Mapping from tables to commands:

Methodology notes (also in the harness README): timings are CUDA-graph replay medians of 50, matching the issue's methodology; the E2E hook requires single-process mode so the sampler patch lands in-process; warmup covers the full batch to compile all batch-size specializations before measurement. For the A/B, the stock side is the released wheel 0.31.0 kernel and the fixed side is that same file with only the zeroth-pass region replaced by this PR's logic — so the comparison isolates the change and no other main-branch drift.

**Update: reworked implementation + shared-protocol benchmark (addresses the review feedback in #61998 and incorporates the fallback design from #62760).**

Rework summary (commit 8e6478c):
1. **Zeroth pass keeps the Gaussian quantile** (the paper's method), but samples **four quarters of the row** instead of tile 0 — the layout bias the issue identified. The stock 0.15 safety discount is kept: with unbiased sampling, the gather fails <1% on real decode rows at every k measured (Qwen3-8B: 0.0%/0.8%/0.8% at k=20/50/64; 7.6% at k=200; 86% only at k=1000).
2. **When the gather under-covers k**, re-gather once at a distribution-free pivot into the per-program buffer, then run the ternary search entirely in the buffer (L2-resident — the fallback shape from #62760):
   - dense rows: the m-th largest of a 2048-lane strided whole-row sample, m = max(8, ceil(4kS/V)) — no distribution assumption, so it covers the skewed rows the Gaussian cannot;
   - sparse rows (grammar masks, where the sample may see no finite logit): the row minimum, which collects every finite candidate — the row is known to hold >= k finite logits (upstream short-circuit), so the buffer always covers k.
3. Small k is untouched relative to main: same read volume (8192 lanes, now in four coalesced segments), same discount, same tight gather.

**Shared protocol, same A800 for all three kernels** (wheel 0.31.0 + single-file swap; captured teacher-forced decode rows, ~250 rows/model; CUDA-graph replay, median of 50; top-k + top-p=0.95):

*Real decode rows (B=64):*

**Architecture note** (to make the tiered structure of the reworked fallback explicit, following the discussion with #62760):

```
zeroth pass: Gaussian quantile over a 4-quarter coalesced sample  (the paper's
             estimator, layout-bias fixed per #62760; stock 0.15 discount)
  ├─ gather covers k  (>99% of real decode rows at every k measured)
  │    → search the gathered buffer (unchanged fast path)
  └─ gather under-covers k
       → tier 2: re-gather once at the order-statistic pivot
         (m-th largest of a 2048-lane strided whole-row sample, 4x margin
          over k — no distribution assumption, covers skewed rows)
         ├─ dense rows (num_finite_total > 2*BLOCK_SIZE): the sample has
         │  ~450+ finite lanes, so the m-th order statistic is reliable
         └─ sparse rows (grammar masks): the sample may hold too few finite
            lanes to estimate anything — take the row minimum instead,
            which collects every finite candidate. The row is guaranteed
            to hold >= k finite logits (upstream num_finite_total <= k
            short-circuit), so this always covers k
       → all ternary-search iterations then run inside the re-gathered
         buffer (L2-resident, #62760's fallback shape)
```

Each tier only pays when the previous one fails: normal rows cost the same as main plus the (already-present) 8192-lane read, now in four segments; skewed rows pay one extra full sweep for the re-gather; sparse rows pay one more. Nothing ever falls back to the 18-iteration full-vocab DRAM search — that path is gone.

Hi @hjh123445, #60104 fixes a separate correctness issue in the standalone top-p block changed here. Sampling four quarters improves the initial estimate, but a sufficiently large unsampled logit can still overflow exp(logits - max_sample) and make top-p keep the whole row. #60104 raises that reference as needed, rescales the accumulated sum, and matches boundary duplicates in probability space.

I'm keeping that normalization repair and its regression tests in #60104. Could we coordinate the overlapping edits so both changes are preserved, whichever lands first?
